topic: Constructive completeness for causal recovery from selected data plus one unbiased external margin.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there a terminating sound-and-complete identification procedure for every finite-state semi-Markovian selection ADMG that decides recoverability of P_x(Y) from exactly P(V|S=1) and one unbiased joint margin P(T0)?

source_refs.claim: IDSB is proved sound for biased P(V|S=1) plus unbiased P(T0), but the paper explicitly leaves completeness of the algorithm unclear.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: This work gives a general identification algorithm for regime-indexed data fusion under systematic selection, but does not state a reduction to one selected conditional law plus one arbitrary unbiased margin.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Do-search is sound for arbitrary incomplete sources, while completeness is inherited only for source classes already characterized by complete do-calculus results.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, Juha Karvanen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim define precisely the two-law input and derive the margin-extension step plus the sound IDSB recursion, but withhold completeness. Ordinary ID and positive gID completeness do not transfer directly because a selected conditional is a normalized ratio involving an unobserved selection mass, whereas P(T0) is only a marginal of the population law. The broader systematic-selection framework has different regime-indexed data objects, and the searched primary sources do not prove that its success rules and failure witnesses specialize to this exact two-source model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite recursive algorithm that returns an arithmetic identifying functional of P(V|S=1) and P(T0) or a graph-indexed pair of compatible finite SCMs with identical input laws and different P_x(Y), with proofs of soundness, completeness, and termination.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces exactly the biased-law-plus-unbiased-margin problem and separates the solved biased-only case from the unresolved external-data completeness boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Confounding and preferential sampling coexist -> a small unbiased covariate margin may restore population information -> IDSB exploits both laws but lacks a completeness theorem -> decide the exact two-source recoverability frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce a multi-source identification problem to ordinary ID subproblems under positivity and prove necessity through a positive linear-system construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem must likewise turn heterogeneous source information into district-level ID calls without losing a completeness certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Use fixing operators and reachable districts to express latent-variable kernels and characterize identifiable interventions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed recursion feeds population kernels reconstructed from the external margin into district fixing.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile fixing-based ADMG functionals into sequentially reweighted and influence-function estimators with limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A returned two-source functional contains ordinary fixing components whose estimator construction should inherit this recursive architecture.

open_problems.open_problem: Can every terminal obstruction of a margin-augmented fixing recursion be converted constructively into two epsilon-interior finite SCMs that agree exactly on P(V|S=1) and P(T0) but disagree on P_x(Y)?

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that positivity breaks the earlier gID completeness proof and replaces it with a sound-and-complete positivity-respecting construction.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Classical ID completeness converts a hedge obstruction into two compatible semi-Markovian models agreeing observationally and disagreeing interventionally.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: The external-margin problem requires simultaneous equality of the selected conditional distribution and unbiased margin, but its proposed algorithm is proved only sound.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: if the source-cover recursion fails, then there exist two finite binary semi-Markovian SCMs
Broad local failure completeness is false on sparse compatibility fibers
The result refutes completeness but does not characterize all identifiable final-return inputs

open_problems.why_unsolved: A classical hedge witness preserves one observational law, and the positive gID construction preserves a collection of interventional source kernels. Here the witness equations must preserve a normalized selected law and a population margin simultaneously while selection probabilities stay away from zero and one. Prior CausalSmith attempts add two concrete hazards: row-face failure can outer-relax the sparse graph-compatible fiber, and terminal graphical failure can conceal support-pooling identification. The first changed proof step is therefore a district-factorized witness system enforcing conditional-law cross-products, P(T0) equalities, strict interior inequalities, and a nonzero query contrast without admitting incompatible latent laws.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A margin-anchored hedge or thicket lemma giving, for each terminal failure configuration, an explicit finite response-function construction and a uniform positive epsilon for two same-input/different-query SCMs, or a counterexample identifying the missing recovery rule.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation is organized around the exact issue that a nominal completeness argument can fail once positivity is imposed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Completeness needs indistinguishable models -> traditional witnesses use structural zeros or an enlarged law space -> positivity and graph compatibility invalidate them -> construct an interior witness that also preserves the external margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate a hedge into paired finite SCMs whose observational laws cancel while the target interventional distribution changes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is the two-source, positivity-strengthened analogue of this classical necessity proof.

method_exemplars.technique: Choose positive conditional probabilities and solve finite equality constraints so every available source law coincides while the target kernel changes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its positivity-respecting synchronization is the nearest machinery for satisfying multiple exact source constraints without zero cells.

open_problems.open_problem: Can Z independent of S given T0 be replaced by a necessary-and-sufficient graph-checkable kernel-separability condition that permits margin-anchored fixing inside a partially selected bidirected district?

source_refs.excerpt: Can district closure be replaced by a strictly weaker graph-checkable kernel-separability condition
Turn the partial-district OEQ into a smallest explicit leakage family, specifying both paired SCMs

open_problems.why_unsolved: The reconstruction P(T0,Z)=P(Z|T0,S=1)P(T0) handles a conditional-independence case, whereas district closure transports whole kernels. When selection reaches only part of a bidirected district, latent dependence can leak through variables not reconstructed by the margin. The first proof step that changes is fixing-kernel invariance: it must characterize exactly when the selected conditional kernels and P(T0) determine the population district kernel rather than assume whole-district invariance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient graphical kernel-separability theorem with an explicit mixed-source fixing formula on success and an epsilon-interior paired-SCM leakage certificate on failure.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves from heterogeneous source information to recursive transportability conditions and precise graphical obstructions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Different sources reveal different causal kernels -> recursive transport needs source-valid kernel moves -> whole-district invariance is sufficient but restrictive -> locate the exact partial-district separability frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt selection-diagram transportability and s-hedge witness arguments to a kernel reconstructed only partly from an external margin.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems ask whether a shifted graphical component can be replaced by information from another population, but the destination has only one unbiased marginal.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite canonical response-function carriers to prove sufficiency and construct alphabet-preserving leakage pairs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Canonical response carriers turn partial-district kernel recovery into exact finite constraints whose target variation can be checked.

method_exemplars.technique: Use source-specific tangent decompositions and cross-fitting for functionals combining conditional and marginal laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful mixed-source fixing formula has distinct selected-sample and margin-sample nuisance contributions.

open_problems.open_problem: For every binary selection ADMG with at most three substantive nodes and every T0, does the mixed-source recursion agree with exact response-function quantifier elimination on identification and nonidentification?

source_refs.excerpt: any failed recursion whose target row lies in the span refutes the fixed-cardinality converse
Replace the unrestricted global response-law simplex with a latent-DAG or district-factorized response-type construction

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior completeness attempts failed because affine row faces and unrestricted response-law simplexes can contain laws that no graph-compatible SCM realizes. An exact small-graph audit must encode district-factorized response types, conditional-selection normalizers, external-margin equalities, and strict positivity in one semialgebraic problem; merely comparing row spans would repeat the false outer-relaxation argument.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A machine-checkable finite classification theorem for all binary instances with at most three substantive nodes, returning either an exact identifying expression or a minimal exact same-input/different-query SCM pair for every query.

writing_exemplar.why: Its finite-model encoding and certificate style show how to present an exhaustive causal classification rather than a simulation study.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete SCMs have finite response-function encodings -> causal queries become exact polynomial problems -> exhaustive small-instance computation can falsify a graphical frontier -> classify every three-node EXT-ID instance.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate deterministic response types, encode observed and causal probabilities polynomially, and solve exact extrema over compatible latent laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The audit is a finite compatibility-and-query optimization problem with selection conditioning and an external margin added.

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordinary ID and hedge witnesses as exact boundary checks for empty-margin and full-population-law degenerations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These boundary cases must reproduce the classical complete identification classification.

open_problems.open_problem: Can arbitrary differentiable EXT-ID functionals be compiled into saturated two-source plug-in estimators with separate influence functions for selected and margin samples and uniformly valid simultaneous confidence regions over fixed positive compact subclasses?

source_refs.claim: The paper bridges graphical identification and estimation for hidden-variable DAGs with influence-function estimators and an algorithm yielding weight-based estimators for ordinary identifiable effects.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: For non-nested ACTG/WIHS/CNICS data fusion, the paper derives weighting, regression, doubly robust estimators, an efficient influence function, and sandwich variance estimators using individual-level target covariates.
source_refs.author: Fan Li, Ashley L. Buchanan, Stephen R. Cole
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C

source_refs.claim: The paper gives doubly robust, asymptotically normal estimators for transporting trial effects using trial outcomes and a target-population covariate sample, not arbitrary graphical two-law functionals.
source_refs.author: Issa J. Dahabreh, Sarah E. Robertson, Lucia C. Petito, Miguel A. Hernan, Jon A. Steingrimsson

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing influence-function compilers concern a single observed ADMG law, while transport estimators generally assume a specific standardization functional and individual-level target covariates. An EXT-ID expression may contain nested sums, products, and ratios of primitives from two independent samples. The missing proof step is a source-aware derivative calculus that tracks each probability table separately, handles shared denominators, and upgrades pointwise asymptotic linearity to uniform joint Gaussian approximation for all returned intervention and outcome cells.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A symbolic derivative theorem assigning selected-source and margin-source influence functions to every differentiable returned arithmetic expression, plus a joint asymptotic linear expansion and uniformly valid simultaneous confidence region on each fixed epsilon-positive compact parameter class.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames estimator compilation as the missing bridge that makes general graphical identification algorithms practically usable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graphical ID returns complicated functionals -> complexity prevents routine estimation -> influence-function compilation bridges identification and inference -> extend that bridge to two independently sampled source laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively convert fixing-based functionals into reweighted estimating equations and influence-function corrections, then prove asymptotic linearity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: EXT-ID outputs use the same sums, products, ratios, and fixing kernels, but their derivatives split across two sources.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the efficient influence function under a non-nested two-sample likelihood and use stacked estimating equations for sandwich variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its likelihood separates study and target-population contributions, the nearest template for source-specific influence functions.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct doubly robust transported-effect estimators and prove consistency and asymptotic normality with separate trial and target samples.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives two-source limit theory for a standardization functional, a base case the general compiler must subsume.

open_problems.open_problem: Given a selection ADMG and target P_x(Y), which inclusion-minimal sets T0 have an unbiased joint margin sufficient for recovery from P(V|S=1), and can all such minimal margins be enumerated with certificates?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives graphical conditions for recoverability when unbiased data are available on a subset of variables, establishing that the externally measured subset changes recoverability.
source_refs.author: Elias Bareinboim, Jin Tian, Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: Examples show how an unbiased subset margin can recover effects beyond biased-only methods, but no complete enumeration of minimal sufficient margins is supplied.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Do-search can recognize additional data sources or assumptions that identify an effect, but does not state a complete minimal-margin theorem for selected conditional data.
source_refs.author: Juha Karvanen, Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature establishes that auxiliary subsets can help and supplies search tools for proposed added sources, but the closest external-margin algorithm is not complete. Minimality is not a d-separation question alone: enlarging P(T0) can unlock population kernels only after latent projection and district fixing, and distinct incomparable margins can support different recovery paths. The targeted scan found no primary-source theorem enumerating all inclusion-minimal T0 for the exact input pair P(V|S=1), P(T0).
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating enumeration algorithm returning every inclusion-minimal sufficient T0 with an identifying functional and, for every rejected subset, a nonidentification certificate showing that its margin cannot recover P_x(Y).

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates unbiased measurement of only a variable subset as a realistic way to repair selection bias.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selected data distort the population law -> a census or pilot measures only a few variables without bias -> some subsets restore recoverability -> determine exactly which smallest subsets suffice.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand an unbiased margin using selection independences, project remaining variables as latent, and recover district factors recursively.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Minimal-margin enumeration repeatedly tests precisely this margin-to-kernel recovery mechanism.

method_exemplars.technique: Search backward over do-calculus rules and available source distributions to identify useful added data objects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its source-design search suggests a branch-and-prune strategy for candidate margins and redundant supersets.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate transported effects and sandwich variances after selecting baseline covariates sufficient for target-population standardization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an applied estimator-and-inference rung for a chosen sufficient margin and exposes its overlap cost.

open_problems.open_problem: When point recovery from P(V|S=1) and P(T0) fails, can one compute sharp finite-state bounds for P_x(Y) that exactly enforce both source laws and attach valid source-aware confidence regions to the bound endpoints?

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal questions with incomplete or selected data can be reduced to polynomial programs and bounded automatically with certified outer approximations and epsilon-sharpness.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Auxiliary population constraints can tighten selection-bias identified sets, and the paper derives confidence intervals for optimal values over estimated feasible sets.
source_refs.author: Matthew J. Tudball, Rachael A. Hughes, Kate Tilling, Jack Bowden, Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: This work develops bounds and doubly robust endpoint estimators for a sensitivity-parameter data-fusion model, not graph-sharp bounds under an exact selected law and unbiased margin.
source_refs.author: Quinn Lanners, Cynthia Rudin, Alexander Volfovsky, Harsh Parikh

open_problems.why_unsolved: Autobounds supplies response-function optimization, while sample-constrained inference accounts for estimated auxiliary constraints. The exact two-source model instead couples an unknown population joint law to an observed conditional law through an unknown selection normalizer. The first technical change is to encode equality of P(V|S=1) and P(T0) as a compact polynomial feasible set without spurious normalized solutions, then propagate independent sampling error from both laws through potentially nonsmooth bound endpoints. The searched literature does not state this graph-specific sharpness-plus-two-source-inference result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equivalent finite polynomial program whose extrema are the sharp lower and upper bounds on every cell of P_x(Y), an epsilon-sharp convergent solver, and asymptotically valid simultaneous confidence regions for the endpoint vector from independent selected and margin samples.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents automated sharp partial identification as the principled fallback when point identification fails in custom discrete causal settings.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Point identification often fails -> hand-derived bounds are brittle in custom data regimes -> response-function programs automate sharp bounds -> specialize the machinery to selected data plus one unbiased margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize finite SCMs by response functions, translate source restrictions and the causal query into polynomials, and optimize by relaxation plus spatial branch-and-bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired identified set is the image of a finite response-function feasible set constrained by two source laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Relax empirically estimated constraints by a sampling-error allowance and invert the optimized criterion for asymptotically valid confidence intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both selected probabilities and external margins are estimated constraints, so endpoint inference must accommodate uncertainty in the feasible set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use efficient-influence-function correction and double machine learning for lower and upper data-fusion bound endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a modern source-aware endpoint-estimation template, though its identified set is sensitivity-based rather than graph-sharp.

open_problems.open_problem: For the ACTG 320 generalization to women, when does the treatment effect remain identified if individual-level WIHS/CNICS target covariates are replaced by only a finite unbiased joint margin P(T0), while the study law is selection-biased and represented by an ADMG?

source_refs.claim: The ACTG 320 analysis generalizes to women using individual-level WIHS covariates under conditional exchangeability, which the authors note is untestable without target outcome information.
source_refs.author: Fan Li, Ashley L. Buchanan, Stephen R. Cole
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C

source_refs.claim: A joint unbiased margin on a subset of covariates can combine with a selection-biased law to recover causal effects beyond generalized adjustment.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The foundational ACTG 320 application standardizes trial results to a target population using covariate information and highlights selection and effect-modification concerns.
source_refs.author: Stephen R. Cole, Elizabeth A. Stuart

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ACTG analyses use individual-level cohort covariates to estimate sampling scores or outcome-standardization distributions and impose conditional exchangeability between study and population. The external-margin graphical framework supplies a weaker data object but allows latent confounding and recursive fixing; its applicability to the ACTG structure is not established in the searched primary sources. The first proof step that changes is replacing the target-sample expectation and sampling-score likelihood by reconstruction of only those population kernels licensed jointly by the selection ADMG and P(T0).
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph- and margin-specific characterization returning either an explicit ACTG target-population treatment-effect functional of the selected study law and P(T0), or two positive SCMs matching those inputs but yielding different effects for women.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact clinical motivation, target populations, data sources, estimand, and practical generalizability concerns for the audit consumer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ACTG participants differ from U.S. women with HIV -> effect modification threatens external validity -> WIHS/CNICS covariates enable standardization under strong exchangeability -> ask what remains recoverable from only audited margins under a selection ADMG.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover P(T0,Z) as P(Z|T0,S=1)P(T0) under the relevant selection independence, then use latent projection and district-factor identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the concrete move that can replace full target-cohort individual data with an unbiased margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Use weighting, regression, and doubly robust estimating equations with a two-sample efficient influence function and sandwich variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest estimation and audit template for the same ACTG 320/WIHS/CNICS consumer, although it observes richer target information.

literature_map:
1. Shpitser–Pearl (AAAI 2006) gives ordinary semi-Markovian ID completeness and hedge witnesses from a full observational law.
2. Huang–Valtorta (UAI 2006; Annals of Mathematics and AI 2008; arXiv:1206.6831) independently establishes completeness of do-calculus for ordinary identification.
3. Bareinboim–Pearl (UAI 2012; arXiv:1210.4842) proves complete z-identification from observational data plus structured surrogate experiments.
4. Bareinboim–Pearl (AAAI 2013; arXiv:1312.7485) gives a complete transportability algorithm across selection diagrams.
5. Bareinboim–Tian–Pearl (AAAI 2014; DOI 10.1609/aaai.v28i1.9074) studies recovery from selected data supplemented by unbiased subset data.
6. Bareinboim–Tian (AAAI 2015) and Correa–Tian–Bareinboim (AAAI 2019; DOI 10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33012744) settle biased-only recovery; the latter defines P(V|S=1)+P(T0), proves IDSB sound, and leaves completeness unclear.
7. Lee–Correa–Bareinboim (UAI 2020) introduces gID; Kivva–Mokhtarian–Etesami–Kiyavash (UAI 2022; arXiv:2206.01081) repairs its positivity problem with a sound-and-complete reduction to ordinary ID.
8. Tikka–Hyttinen–Karvanen (JSS 2021; arXiv:1902.01073) supplies sound do-search over arbitrary incomplete sources, but completeness transfers only from already complete source classes.
9. Lee–Ghassami–Shpitser (UAI 2024; arXiv:2404.06602) develops a general algorithm for systematic-selection data fusion; no explicit reduction to the one-selected-law/one-margin problem was found.
10. Richardson–Evans–Robins–Shpitser (arXiv:1701.06686) supplies the fixing and reachable-district language for recursive external-margin recovery.
11. Bhattacharya–Nabi–Shpitser (JMLR 2022; arXiv:2003.12659) compiles ordinary ADMG identification into influence-function estimators, but not source-separated derivatives for selected-plus-margin samples.
12. Li–Buchanan–Cole (JRSS C 2022; arXiv:2103.04907) gives EIF/sandwich ACTG 320 transport analyses with individual WIHS/CNICS covariates and flags conditional exchangeability as untestable without target outcomes.
13. Duarte et al. (JASA 2024; arXiv:2109.13471), Tudball et al. (Biometrika 2023; arXiv:1906.10159), and Lanners et al. (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv:2505.24296) provide complementary sharp-bound, auxiliary-constraint-inference, and fusion-endpoint machinery.
